title: Hourly GPU utilization -> hiring trigger matrix
content:
Purpose
---
Compact operational spreadsheet-style playbook linking observed hourly GPU utilization to near-term hiring triggers and price-sensitivity scenarios. Designed as an operational tool for Finance + Capacity Planning to translate utilization telemetry into hiring/credit/burst decisions and pricing experiments. Draft — ask for numbers validation from SRE and Prod Ops.

One-sentence summary
---
If 7-day rolling hourly-GPU-util > 75% during business-hours (UTC−8) AND 30-day revenue-per-GPU-hour < $60, signal for prioritized hiring / spot-reserve purchase; otherwise consider price-preserve experiments before scaling HC.

Assumptions (anchor numbers)
---
- Average GPU type: A100 80GB-equivalent (total infra cost incl. amortized HW, power, SW license) = $2.25 / GPU-hour (current internal blended).
- Add-on infra & ops overhead (network, storage, SRE) = $0.85 / GPU-hour.
- Total fully-burdened infra cost per GPU-hour = $3.10.
- Average throughput (production tokens) per GPU-hour (baseline mix) = 9M tokens.
- Revenue per 1k tokens (avg across hosted API mix today) = $0.025 -> => revenue per GPU-hour ≈ $225. (Used for sanity checks; breakouts by route below.)
- Fully-loaded junior inference engineer hire (ramp 3 months) = $160k / year -> monthly cost ≈ $13.3k (on-target fully-burdened w/benefits and hiring overhead ~1.35x).

Quick capacity math (useful conversions)
---
- 1 FTE SRE / infra (on-call rotation) supports ~45–60 GPUs depending on service model. Use 50 GPUs / FTE as working baseline.
- Headcount-to-GPU mapping (prod ops): 1 Capacity Engineer per 50 GPUs. 1 Model Ops per 75 GPUs.

Trigger matrix (operational rules)
---
Columns: metric | threshold | suggested action | priority | owner
- 7d rolling GPU util (business hrs) | >75% | Open hiring requisition for Capacity Eng (1x), enable burst spot-bid reserve 12–24wks | P0 | Finance + Infra
- 7d rolling GPU util (business hrs) | 60–75% | Schedule spot-reserve trial, reevaluate cache/batch knobs, hold hires (monitor 14 days) | P1 | Infra + Product
- 7d rolling GPU util (business hrs) | <60% | No hires; consider price or quota experiments to drive uptake | P2 | Growth + Pricing
- 30d rev / GPU-hour (rolling) | < $90 and util > 60% | Favor price-preserve: slow hires and test 10–15% price decrease on mid-tier segments | P1 | Finance + Growth
- 30d rev / GPU-hour (rolling) | < $45 and util > 70% | Strong consideration for burst capacity buys + negotiation on cloud commitments (buy vs hire trade) | P0 | Finance + Procurement

Headcount phasing (quarterly sprints, illustrative)
---
- Q1 2026: +2 Capacity Eng (sourced contractors), +1 Ops Finance analyst (12w ramp) — contingency: convert to FTE if utilization persists >80% for 6 weeks.
- Q2 2026: +1 Model Ops, +1 Product Ops (on-call offset). Targeted only if 3-month avg util >72% and revenue per GPU-hour >= $70.
- Q3 2026: Hiring freeze review — only critical patches or SLA-mandated hires.

Micro-scenarios: pricing sensitivity experiments
---
We propose three short experiments (4–6 weeks each) tied to concrete metrics and traffic cohorts. Each experiment must be A/B with internal route tagging so product metrics correlate directly to GPU-hour demand.
1) Volume-stimulus (discount): -15% price on ‘standard’ route for 4 weeks. Hypothesis: elasticity = 1.6 => demand +24% -> GPU-hours +24%. Metric: change in 14-day rolling GPU-hours and revenue per GPU-hour.
2) Price-preserve (quota gating): keep price → raise quota for mid-tier users (pilot). Hypothesis: revenue per GPU-hour increases 8–12% by shifting heavy tail off hosted.
3) Quality-led upsell (higher-price offering): introduce small premium for better latency SLA (>$X) targeting enterprise customers; low expected volume but higher rev/GPU-hour.

Decision rules connecting price experiments to hiring
---
- If experiment 1 (discount) increases GPU-hours by >15% and rev/GPU-hour stays > $70, approve 1 additional Capacity Eng (contractor -> FTE conversion pipeline start).
- If rev/GPU-hour declines to < $45 across 30d, pause hiring and initiate cost-side measures (aggressive quantization trials, extra prefix cache policies).

Cost vs hire quick model (back-of-envelope)
---
- Hiring cost per Capacity Eng (first 12 months fully-burdened) = $160k. If 1 FTE supports 50 GPUs, cost per GPU-year = $160k / 50 = $3.2k ≈ $8.77 / GPU-day ≈ $0.36 / GPU-hour.
- Compare to cloud commitment: one-year reserved equivalent amortized saving vs spot/ondemand must be > 0.36 / GPU-hour to justify hire purely on labor grounds.
- When util > 78% and revenue per GPU-hour > $90, expected marginal revenue > marginal cost -> hire is favorable.

Example mini-table: (numbers illustrative)
---
Period | Avg util (B-hrs) | Rev / GPU-hr | 7d util trend | Action
Nov-2025 | 69% | $82 | +3% | Spot-reserve trial, monitor 14d
Dec-2025 | 77% | $74 | +9% | Open contractor requisition (1x), run pricing-experiment A
Jan-2026 | 83% | $68 | +5% | Convert contractor to FTE? Consider mix: buy spot reserve + 1 FTE

Operational playbook (short checklist)
---
- Data: Ensure 1h granularity GPU util, rev per GPU-hour by route, 7d and 30d rolling windows. Owner: Infra analytics.
- Communication: Finance issues hiring memo with scenario supporting numbers and straight-line impact on monthly burn. Owner: Finance.
- Procurement: If triggered for reserved capacity, run cloud-comparison TCO (3 vendors) within 7 business days. Owner: Procurement.
- Growth: Coordinate A/B cohort tags and rollout for pricing experiments. Owner: Growth.

Risk & mitigation
---
- Risk: Short-lived utilization spike from small cohort (tests) causes premature hire. Mitigation: require sustained >72% util for minimum 21 calendar days before opening permanent req.
- Risk: Price test cannibalizes high-margin enterprise traffic. Mitigation: route segmentation and exclude enterprise from discount cohorts.

Open questions / TODOs
---
- Validate blended infra cost per GPU-hour with Infra Finance (Aaron).
- Confirm true FTE-to-GPU support ratio across Dedicated vs Hosted (SRE to confirm).
- Build per-route rev / GPU-hour breakdown for last 90 days (sliced by customer tier).
- Decide approval authority: are we OK with Finance + Head of Infra greenlight for 1 contractor hire, or require CFO + Head of People?

Notes to reviewers
---
- This doc intentionally mixes heuristic thresholds and economic back-of-envelope numbers to be actionable at the weekly capacity review. Please flag any hard constraints (e.g., hiring freeze) that should veto triggers.
- I left some margin numbers conservative; if Infra reports lower CPU+storage overhead we can tighten hire signal.

Appendix: quick references
---
- Relevant confluence playbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/FIN/Runway+Playbooks+2026
- JIRA epic for pricing experiments: JIRA-FIN-1421
- Infra analytics dashboard: ops.redwood.ai/dash/gpu-util (internal)

End.
